narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model estimated a 50.9% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a borderline but adverse risk estimate: it does not say failure is certain, but it was high enough for the admissions decision to go against you.

The most influential factor was your third-year class standing, and it actually pushed toward passing. Your fifth-decile standing was close to the accepted-student average of about 5.8, so it was not the main weakness. The second most influential factor was your admissions test score, which pushed toward failure; your score of 30.5 is well below the accepted-student average of 37.2. The third factor, your undergraduate GPA, also pushed toward failure; at 3.00 it is below the accepted average of 3.23. Even though your strongest single signal helped you, these two academic indicators raised the predicted risk enough to produce the slight failure estimate.

To improve your next application, focus on strengthening the areas that pushed toward failure: consider retaking the admissions test after preparation, take additional coursework or otherwise demonstrate improved academic readiness, and seek advising on how to present your record and any bar-readiness steps you have taken.
